title: Double-crested cormorants over Monterey Bay, California, United States
caption: Life along the flyway
subtitle: World Migratory Bird Day
description:
World Migratory Bird Day celebrates one of nature's greatest journeys. Observed each year in May and October, the global campaign reflects migration patterns around the world and highlights the importance of protecting the habitats and flyways that birds depend on. 'Every Bird Counts—Your Observations Matter!' is the 2026 theme, emphasising how observations by individuals and communities can contribute to bird research, monitoring and conservation, helping scientists better understand migration.
Today's image captures double-crested cormorants flying above the waves of Monterey Bay, California. Widespread across North America, these adaptable seabirds may migrate or remain year-round, depending on the population. Along California's coast, bays, wetlands and estuaries provide important habitat for birds traveling the Pacific Flyway. For many species, these ecosystems support journeys spanning vast distances. Each sighting helps reveal these migrations and reminds us that even a single bird can be part of a much larger story.

title: Glade Creek Grist Mill, Babcock State Park, West Virginia, USA
caption: Where autumn turns the wheel
subtitle: Glade Creek Grist Mill, Babcock State Park, West Virginia
description:
Surrounded by a patchwork of red, orange and gold, Glade Creek Grist Mill stands above the rocky waters of Glade Creek in West Virginia's Babcock State Park, United States. Although it looks like a relic from the pioneer era, the mill is actually a carefully crafted tribute to Appalachia's milling heritage.
Completed in 1976, the mill was built using parts salvaged from several historic gristmills once scattered across West Virginia, bringing together pieces of the state's rural past in a single working structure. Water from Glade Creek still turns the wheel and powers traditional grain-grinding demonstrations, offering visitors a glimpse into a way of life once common throughout the Appalachian Mountains.
The mill may be the park's most recognisable landmark, but it is only part of the story. Each autumn, Babcock State Park's forests transform into a mosaic of brilliant colour, framing waterfalls, rocky streambeds and kilometres of hiking trails. Together, the landscape and mill create an enduring symbol of Appalachian history, craftsmanship and natural beauty.

title: Baker Lake near East Bolton, Quebec
caption: Hearts filled with gratitude
subtitle: Thanksgiving Day
description:
Pull up a chair, pass the pie and make some room for gratitude. Thanksgiving in Canada has a story that goes back much further than the holiday table. This holiday is rooted in harvest traditions, with people gathering to give thanks. Its history is not tied to one single event, although an early celebration is associated with English explorer Martin Frobisher. In 1578, after his expedition made a safe passage across the Atlantic and reached what is now Nunavut, Frobisher held a celebratory feast. Over time, Thanksgiving evolved into a national holiday centred on the harvest and spending time with loved ones.
Today, a shared meal might feature turkey, stuffing, vegetables, cranberry sauce and pumpkin pie, while the long weekend also offers time for visits, walks and catching up. Baker Lake near East Bolton, Quebec, provides a fitting autumn backdrop, with colourful trees reflected in the water. On a holiday about appreciating what we have, what are you thankful for?

title: Plitvice Lakes National Park, Croatia
caption: A symphony in blue and green
subtitle: Plitvice Lakes National Park, Croatia
description:
Water seems to be everywhere at Plitvice Lakes National Park in Croatia. Sixteen terraced lakes are linked by a network of waterfalls, streams and cascades that wind through forested limestone canyons. The constantly changing colours of the water, ranging from emerald green to deep blue, are shaped by minerals, sunlight and ever-changing reflections. Established in 1949, Plitvice Lakes is Croatia's oldest and largest national park. The landscape is famous for its tufa barriers, natural limestone formations created as mineral-rich water deposits calcium carbonate over centuries. These barriers continue to grow and change, gradually transforming the park's waterfalls and lakes.
Recognised as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1979, Plitvice protects one of Europe's most remarkable freshwater ecosystems. Wooden walkways weave across the water, bringing visitors close to cascades, tranquil pools and forested shores where nature continues to reshape the landscape. Here, lakes, waterfalls and woodlands come together in a scene that feels almost otherworldly.

title: Brown bear in Silver Salmon Creek, Lake Clark National Park and Preserve, Alaska, United States
caption: Catch, eat, repeat
subtitle: Brown bear in Lake Clark National Park and Preserve, Alaska, USA
description:
The season of big meals, bigger bellies and stocking up for winter is here. In Alaska, brown bears at Lake Clark National Park and Preserve make the most of the food still available in October. They feed on fish, sedges, berries, roots, clams and other foods to build up fat reserves. Some can weigh more than 450 kilograms before entering their dens for hibernation. That stored fat helps them survive the winter, when they do not eat or drink.
Silver Salmon Creek is a bear buffet, and bear-watching is a popular activity in this national park. One of the nation's most remote units, Lake Clark National Park and Preserve spans more than 16,000 square kilometres and can be reached by plane or boat. Its Cook Inlet coast is also home to moose, wolves, foxes and marine mammals. If you're planning a visit, come prepared for wilderness, wildlife and a place where the bears get one of the best tables.

title: View of the Wroclaw Market Square from the Witches' Bridge in Wroclaw, Poland
caption: Bridges, rooftops and twilight
subtitle: Market Square from the Witches' Bridge, Wroclaw, Poland
description:
As twilight settles over Wroclaw, golden light spills across rooftops, church towers and one of Central Europe's most striking historic centres. This southwestern Polish city spans islands and waterways linked by more than 100 bridges, blending medieval architecture with vibrant modern life. At its heart is Rynek, a lively Market Square established in the 13th century and home to the Gothic Old Town Hall, one of Wroclaw's most recognisable landmarks.
Today's view was captured from the Witches' Bridge, also known as the Bridge of the Penitents, a footbridge connecting the towers of St. Mary Magdalene Church. Suspended about 45 metres above the ground, it offers sweeping views of the Old Town's colourful facades, winding streets and the bustling Market Square below. From centuries-old churches and riverside promenades to museums and cafés, Wroclaw rewards visitors with something new at every turn. After sunset, the city is especially enchanting as its historic centre glows beneath the evening sky.

title: Maligne Lake, Jasper National Park, Alberta
caption: Under a blanket of stars
subtitle: Jasper Dark Sky Festival is here
description:
Why settle for a planetarium ceiling when Jasper can give you the real thing? That's rather the point of the Jasper Dark Sky Festival, which kicks off today and runs until October 25. The annual event grew from celebrations surrounding Jasper National Park's 2011 designation as a Dark Sky Preserve. The idea is simple: protect natural darkness, then give people plenty of reasons to appreciate it.
Expect telescope viewing, astronomy talks, planetarium shows, science activities and guided experiences designed to make the night sky a little less mysterious. Songwriter Afie Jurvanen, aka Bahamas, takes the stage before 'Love Letters From the Moon,' a drone show that turns the night sky into the next act. Other sessions bring astronomers and their telescopes outdoors for closer looks at the Moon and distant celestial objects. And when daylight returns, Maligne Lake supplies another spectacular change of scenery. At 22 kilometres long, this glacier-fed lake is the largest natural lake in the Canadian Rockies.

title: Life-size replica of Chauvet Cave art in Vallon-Pont-d'Arc, France
caption: The past, unearthed
description: Some discoveries start with a shovel. Others start with a drawing on a cave wall. International Archaeology Day celebrates both the detective work and the evidence behind them. Organised by the Archaeological Institute of America, this annual event began in 2011 and became International Archaeology Day in 2013 as participation expanded worldwide. Today, it brings archaeology closer to the public through talks, museum programmes, site visits, simulated digs and hands-on activities.
